questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Position of a gene on a chromosome
questions.question: The fixed position of a gene on a chromosome is called its ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) locus
Why: A locus is the site a gene occupies on a chromosome.
Why not the others: (B) an allele is one form of a gene; (C) the centromere joins sister chromatids; (D) a chiasma is a crossing-over point.
Key point: Locus = address of a gene.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Name for a young female not yet calved
questions.question: A young female cow that has not yet given birth to a calf is called a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) heifer
Why: A heifer is a young female that has not calved.
Why not the others: (B) a bullock and (C) a steer are castrated males; (D) a ram is a male sheep.
Key point: Heifer → cow after first calving.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.question:
Match List-I (Structure) with List-II (Use).

List-I
(A) Mist chamber
(B) Polyhouse
(C) Shade net house
(D) Hot bed

List-II
(I) Cuts down light for shade-loving plants
(II) A heated bed for raising early seedlings in cold weather
(III) Keeps humidity high to root cuttings
(IV) Protected cultivation under a plastic-film cover
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: A mist chamber keeps humidity high to root cuttings (III). A polyhouse gives protected cultivation under plastic film (IV). A shade net house cuts down light (I). A hot bed is heated to raise early seedlings (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps mist chamber and polyhouse. Option (B) swaps shade net and hot bed. Option (D) swaps polyhouse and shade net.
Key point: Nursery structures control humidity, light and temperature.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Fisheries
questions.question: Fish is valued in the diet mainly as a rich source of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) protein
Why: Fish flesh is rich in easily digested protein.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not supplied by fish.
Key point: Fish — high-quality protein.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Irrigation needs of soils and crops
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Crop water requirement includes evapotranspiration, application losses and special needs such as puddling.
(B) Rice generally needs more water than wheat over its growing season.
(C) Sandy soils are best irrigated lightly and often.
(D) Clay soils need lighter and more frequent irrigations than sandy soils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are true. (D) is false: clay holds more water, so it can take heavier irrigations at longer intervals; sandy soil needs light, frequent ones.
Why not the others: Option (A) leaves out (C). Options (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Match the depth and interval of irrigation to the soil.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.question: In crop production, which of the following describes a 'weed'?
options: A) a plant growing where it is not wanted
B) any plant that has no flowers
C) a plant that grows only in water
D) any plant that is poisonous to animals
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) a plant growing where it is not wanted
Why: A weed is a plant out of place, competing with the crop for light, water and nutrients.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) do not define a weed.
Key point: Weed = plant out of place.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.sub_topic: Vegetable crops — which statements are wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Okra belongs to the family Solanaceae.
(B) Tomato belongs to the family Solanaceae.
(C) Cucumber is a cucurbit.
(D) Garlic is commercially propagated by true seed.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) and (D) only
Why: (B) and (C) are true. (A) is false: okra belongs to Malvaceae. (D) is false: garlic is propagated by cloves.
Why not the others: Option (B) calls true statements wrong. Option (C) misses statement (D). Option (D) calls the true statement (C) wrong.
Key point: Okra — Malvaceae; garlic — cloves.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Air temperature usually reaches its daily maximum in the early afternoon.
(B) Air temperature generally falls as altitude increases.
(C) Cold waves can injure crops such as mustard and potato.
(D) The daily minimum temperature usually occurs around noon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are true. (D) is false: the minimum usually occurs just before sunrise, after the ground has lost heat all night.
Why not the others: Option (A) leaves out (C). Options (C) and (D) include the false statement (D).
Key point: Maximum in early afternoon; minimum just before sunrise.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary (major) plant nutrient?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Potassium
Why: Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are the primary nutrients, needed in the largest amounts.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are micronutrients.
Key point: N, P and K — primary nutrients.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Linkage and crossing over — which statements are wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Genes lying close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together.
(B) Crossing over takes place during prophase I of meiosis.
(C) Crossing over occurs between sister chromatids of the same chromosome.
(D) The farther apart two linked genes are, the less often crossing over separates them.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) and (B) are true. (C) is false: crossing over is between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. (D) is false: genes farther apart are separated more often.
Why not the others: Options (A) and (B) call true statements wrong. Option (C) misses statement (D).
Key point: Linkage keeps genes together; distance raises the chance of crossing over.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.question: Milk that is concentrated by removing part of its water, mixed with sugar and canned is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) sweetened condensed milk
Why: Sweetened condensed milk is evaporated milk with added sugar, which also helps preserve it.
Why not the others: (A) khoa is a solid mass made by open-pan boiling; (B) is dried skim milk; (C) ghee is clarified butterfat.
Key point: Condensed milk keeps because of high sugar and low water.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.question: Mixed farming means:
options: A) growing crops and rearing livestock together on the same farm
B) growing two crops in alternate rows in the same field
C) growing a crop only once in two years on the same land
D) growing crops without any chemical inputs at all
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) growing crops and rearing livestock together on the same farm
Why: Mixed farming combines crop production with livestock, so each supports the other.
Why not the others: (B) is intercropping; (C) is fallowing; (D) is organic farming.
Key point: Mixed farming = crops + animals.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.question: In hypogeal germination, the cotyledons stay below the soil. Which of the following shows hypogeal germination?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Pea
Why: In pea the epicotyl lengthens, so the cotyledons remain underground.
Why not the others: (B) cotton, (C) castor and (D) French bean show epigeal germination, with cotyledons raised above the soil.
Key point: Pea, gram and maize — hypogeal.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of making vermicompost in the correct order.
(A) Harvesting the compost after about two months
(B) Spreading the waste in a shaded bed
(C) Releasing earthworms into the bed
(D) Partly decomposing the organic waste for two to three weeks
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (D), (B), (C), (A)
Why: The waste is first partly decomposed (D), spread in a shaded bed (B), earthworms are released (C), and the compost is harvested after about two months (A).
Why not the others: Option (A) spreads the waste before it is decomposed. Option (C) releases worms before the bed is made. Option (D) harvests before the worms are added.
Key point: Pre-decompose → bed → worms → harvest.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of making silage in the correct order.
(A) Chopping the fodder into small pieces
(B) Sealing the silo airtight
(C) Cutting the fodder crop at the right stage
(D) Filling and pressing the fodder in the silo
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: The crop is cut at the right stage (C), chopped (A), filled and pressed to drive out air (D), and the silo is sealed (B) so that it ferments without air.
Why not the others: Option (A) chops before cutting. Option (B) fills before chopping. Option (C) seals before filling.
Key point: Silage needs air excluded for good fermentation.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question: Which of the following vegetables is a cool-season (winter) crop in the plains of north India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Cabbage
Why: Cabbage grows best in cool weather and is planted in winter in the north Indian plains.
Why not the others: (A) okra, (C) bottle gourd and (D) cowpea are warm-season crops.
Key point: Cole crops are cool-season vegetables.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.question: In rainfed areas, a farm pond is dug mainly to:
options: A) drain all the rainwater quickly out of the farm area
B) raise fish only, with no use at all for the crops
C) store runoff for life-saving irrigation during dry spells
D) recharge the deep aquifers that supply water to cities
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) store runoff for life-saving irrigation during dry spells
Why: A farm pond collects runoff in the rainy season; the stored water saves the crop during a dry spell.
Why not the others: (A) is the opposite; (B) fish may be raised, but the main aim is water for crops; (D) is not its main purpose.
Key point: Farm ponds = rainwater harvesting for protective irrigation.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question:
Match List-I (Type of erosion) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Splash erosion
(B) Sheet erosion
(C) Gully erosion
(D) Rill erosion

List-II
(I) A thin, even layer of topsoil is removed from the slope
(II) Raindrops strike bare soil and detach particles
(III) Small channels form that can be smoothed out by tillage
(IV) Deep channels form that farm implements cannot cross
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: Splash erosion is caused by raindrop impact (II). Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer (I). Gullies are deep channels (IV). Rills are small channels that tillage can smooth (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps splash and sheet. Option (B) swaps gully and rill. Option (C) swaps sheet and gully.
Key point: Splash → sheet → rill → gully as erosion worsens.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question: Dehorning of calves is best done:
options: A) within the first few weeks after birth
B) after the animal's first calving
C) when the animal is about five years old
D) only in old animals that have stopped milking
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) within the first few weeks after birth
Why: In young calves the horn buds are small and not yet joined to the skull, so dehorning is easy and less painful.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are too late; the grown horn is hard to remove.
Key point: Dehorn early, at the horn-bud stage.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question:
Match List-I (Weather hazard) with List-II (Description).

List-I
(A) Frost
(B) Hailstorm
(C) Heat wave
(D) Drought

List-II
(I) Temperature stays well above normal for several days
(II) Temperature falls to 0 °C or below and ice forms on surfaces
(III) A long period of rainfall well below normal
(IV) Balls of ice fall from tall cumulonimbus clouds
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)
Why: Frost forms at 0 °C or below (II). Hail falls from cumulonimbus clouds (IV). A heat wave is a spell of very high temperature (I). Drought is a long rainfall deficit (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps frost and hailstorm. Option (B) swaps heat wave and drought. Option (D) swaps hailstorm and heat wave.
Key point: Each hazard needs its own crop-protection advice.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Lines of equal rainfall on a map
questions.question: On a weather map, isohyets are lines joining places that have equal:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) rainfall
Why: Isohyets connect points that received the same amount of rainfall.
Why not the others: (B) equal temperature lines are isotherms; (C) equal pressure lines are isobars; (D) humidity lines are not called isohyets.
Key point: Isohyet — rain; isotherm — temperature; isobar — pressure.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Utility of four Indian cattle breeds
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Red Sindhi is a dairy breed of cattle.
(B) Hariana is a dual-purpose breed of cattle.
(C) Kankrej is a dual-purpose breed from Gujarat.
(D) Deoni is a dual-purpose breed from Maharashtra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B), (C) and (D)
Why: All four statements are true.
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (C) each leave out at least one true statement.
Key point: Indian breeds are grouped as dairy, draught or dual-purpose.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of Gram staining of bacteria in the correct order.
(A) Counterstaining with safranin
(B) Staining with crystal violet
(C) Washing with alcohol (decolourising)
(D) Treating with Gram's iodine
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (D), (C), (A)
Why: The smear is stained with crystal violet (B), fixed with Gram's iodine (D), decolourised with alcohol (C) and counterstained with safranin (A). Gram-positive cells stay violet; Gram-negative cells turn pink.
Why not the others: Option (B) adds iodine before the stain. Option (C) decolourises before the iodine. Option (D) counterstains before decolourising.
Key point: Crystal violet → iodine → alcohol → safranin.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.sub_topic: Milk and its forms — which statement is wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Toned milk is made by adding only water to buffalo milk.
(B) Cream rises to the top of milk because fat is lighter than the rest of the milk.
(C) Cow milk is about 87 percent water.
(D) Skim milk is milk from which most of the fat has been removed.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) only
Why: (A) is false: toned milk is made by mixing buffalo milk with skim milk powder and water, to about 3% fat. (B), (C) and (D) are true.
Why not the others: Statements (B), (C) and (D) are correct.
Key point: Toned milk = buffalo milk + skim milk powder + water.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Animal diseases and their causal agents
questions.question:
Match List-I (Disease) with List-II (Type of causal agent).

List-I
(A) Anthrax
(B) Rabies
(C) Ringworm
(D) Babesiosis

List-II
(I) Protozoan spread by ticks
(II) Fungus
(III) Virus
(IV) Bacterium
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Anthrax is caused by a bacterium, *Bacillus anthracis* (IV). Rabies is viral (III). Ringworm is fungal (II). Babesiosis is a tick-borne protozoan disease (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps anthrax and rabies. Option (C) swaps rabies and ringworm. Option (D) swaps ringworm and babesiosis.
Key point: Knowing the agent decides the treatment.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question: Aam papad, a dried fruit leather, is made from the pulp of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) mango
Why: 'Aam' means mango; its pulp with sugar is spread in thin layers and sun-dried.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not used for aam papad.
Key point: Aam papad = dried mango pulp.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question: Microorganisms that cause disease are called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) pathogens
Why: A pathogen is any organism that causes disease.
Why not the others: (A) saprophytes and (D) decomposers feed on dead matter; (B) symbionts live in partnership with a host.
Key point: Pathogen = disease-causer.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Term for the visible expression of a trait
questions.question: The observable expression of a trait, such as tall or dwarf plants, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) phenotype
Why: Phenotype is the visible or measurable character of an organism.
Why not the others: (A) genotype is its genetic make-up; (C) karyotype is its chromosome set as seen under a microscope; (D) genome is all its DNA.
Key point: Genotype + environment → phenotype.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question: The plough layer of one hectare is 15 cm deep, and its bulk density is 1.5 tonnes per cubic metre. What is the weight of this furrow slice?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 2,250 tonnes
Why: Step 1: volume = 10,000 m² × 0.15 m = 1,500 m³.
Step 2: weight = 1,500 × 1.5 = 2,250 tonnes (about 2.25 million kg).
Why not the others: (A) is ten times too small; (B) is the volume, not the weight; (D) is ten times too large.
Key point: Furrow slice of 1 ha ≈ 2.25 million kg.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Group made up of sheep breeds
questions.question: Which group consists only of Indian sheep breeds?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Nellore, Deccani and Chokla
Why: Nellore (Andhra Pradesh), Deccani (Maharashtra) and Chokla (Rajasthan) are sheep breeds.
Why not the others: (A) are cattle breeds; (B) are goat breeds; (D) are buffalo breeds.
Key point: Chokla gives fine carpet wool.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (Test) with List-II (Result).

List-I
(A) Iodine test
(B) Benedict's test
(C) Biuret test
(D) Sudan III test

List-II
(I) Brick-red precipitate with reducing sugars
(II) Red stain with fats and oils
(III) Blue-black colour with starch
(IV) Violet colour with proteins
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Iodine turns starch blue-black (III). Benedict's reagent gives a brick-red precipitate with reducing sugars (I). Biuret reagent turns violet with proteins (IV). Sudan III stains fats red (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps iodine and Benedict's. Option (C) swaps Benedict's and biuret. Option (D) swaps biuret and Sudan III.
Key point: Simple colour tests identify the main biomolecules.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Why cattle shed floors slope to a drain
questions.question: Why is the floor of a cattle shed built with a gentle slope towards a drain?
options: A) Because a sloping floor makes the animals give much more milk
B) Because cattle are unable to stand comfortably on a level floor
C) Because urine and washing water run off and the floor stays dry
D) Because the slope keeps flies, ticks and mites out of the shed
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because urine and washing water run off and the floor stays dry
Why: A slope of about 1 in 40 to 1 in 60 drains urine and water away, keeping the floor dry and clean and reducing hoof problems and disease.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the reason.
Key point: Dry, clean floors keep animals healthy.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Method not used for self-pollinated crops
questions.question: Breeders choose methods to suit the crop's mode of pollination. Which of the following is NOT a method used for breeding self-pollinated crops?
options: A) Pure-line selection from a landrace
B) Mass selection of desirable plants
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Development of synthetic varieties
Why: Synthetic varieties are made by inter-crossing several lines of a cross-pollinated crop, such as maize or pearl millet.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are standard methods for self-pollinated crops.
Key point: Synthetics and composites are for cross-pollinated crops.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question: Edible mushrooms such as the button mushroom belong to the group:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) fungi
Why: Mushrooms are the fruiting bodies of fungi; they have no chlorophyll and feed on organic matter.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are other groups; mushrooms cannot photosynthesise.
Key point: Mushrooms are fungi grown on straw or compost.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question:
Match List-I (Term) with List-II (Meaning).

List-I
(A) Pasteurisation
(B) Sterilisation
(C) Fermentation
(D) Osmotic dehydration

List-II
(I) Killing all microbes, as in canning above 100 °C
(II) Microbes convert sugars into acid or alcohol
(III) Fruit pieces partly dried by soaking in sugar syrup
(IV) Heating below 100 °C to kill most harmful microbes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(III)
Why: Pasteurisation heats below 100 °C (IV). Sterilisation kills all microbes (I). Fermentation turns sugars into acid or alcohol (II). Osmotic dehydration draws water out in sugar syrup (III).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps pasteurisation and sterilisation. Option (C) swaps sterilisation and fermentation. Option (D) swaps fermentation and osmotic dehydration.
Key point: Mild heat pasteurises; strong heat sterilises.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question: A non-protein helper, such as a metal ion, that an enzyme needs in order to work is called a ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) cofactor
Why: Cofactors such as Mg²⁺ or Zn²⁺, or organic coenzymes, are needed for many enzymes to be active.
Why not the others: (A) the substrate is acted on; (B) the product is formed; (C) an inhibitor slows the enzyme.
Key point: Enzyme + cofactor = active enzyme.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question: Why are DNA and RNA called nucleic 'acids'?
options: A) Because they contain many free amino groups
B) Because they are found only in acidic parts of the cell
C) Because their phosphate groups release hydrogen ions
D) Because they are made largely of citric acid
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Because their phosphate groups release hydrogen ions
Why: The phosphate groups in the sugar–phosphate backbone give up hydrogen ions, so the molecules are acidic; 'nucleic' comes from the nucleus where they were found.
Why not the others: (A) amino groups are basic; (B) and (D) are not true.
Key point: Phosphate backbone → acidic nature.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.question: Rows of tall trees such as shisham or eucalyptus are planted along the edge of an orchard to:
options: A) supply fruit to the market earlier than the main crop
B) attract pollinating insects away from the fruit trees
C) increase the shade on the fruit trees all day
D) protect the orchard from strong, hot or cold winds
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) protect the orchard from strong, hot or cold winds
Why: A windbreak slows the wind, reducing flower and fruit drop, branch breakage and water loss.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the purpose.
Key point: Windbreaks shelter orchards.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Subject that is not a branch of agriculture
questions.question: Agriculture is studied in several branches. Which of the following is NOT a branch of agriculture?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Ornithology
Why: Ornithology is the study of birds, a branch of zoology.
Why not the others: (A) agronomy (field crops), (B) horticulture (garden crops) and (C) animal husbandry (livestock) are branches of agriculture.
Key point: Agronomy, horticulture and animal husbandry are core branches.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.question: The word 'agriculture' comes from the Latin words 'ager' and 'cultura'. What does 'ager' mean?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Field
Why: 'Ager' means field and 'cultura' means cultivation, so agriculture is cultivation of the field.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the meaning.
Key point: Agriculture = field + cultivation.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question: In plant breeding, a backcross is:
options: A) a cross between two unrelated pure-line varieties
B) self-pollination of the F₁ plants for one more season
C) a cross of the F₁ hybrid with one of its parents
D) a cross between two different single-cross F₁ hybrids
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) a cross of the F₁ hybrid with one of its parents
Why: A backcross mates the F₁ (or a later generation) with one of its parents, often to transfer one gene into a good variety.
Why not the others: (A) is a single cross; (B) is selfing; (D) is a double cross.
Key point: Backcross = F₁ × parent.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.question: Water-use efficiency of a crop is expressed as:
options: A) water applied per hectare per day
B) depth of water standing in the field
C) water lost by deep percolation per irrigation
D) crop yield produced per unit of water used
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) crop yield produced per unit of water used
Why: Water-use efficiency is the yield obtained per unit of water used, for example kg per hectare-mm.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) measure water quantities, not the return per unit of water.
Key point: Higher yield per drop = higher water-use efficiency.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.sub_topic: Quality not expected in good seed
questions.question: Farmers are advised to buy good-quality seed. Which of the following is NOT a quality of good seed?
options: B) Presence of many weed seeds
C) Genetic purity of the variety
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Presence of many weed seeds
Why: Good seed should be free from weed seeds, which would add weeds to the field.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are all qualities of good seed.
Key point: Good seed is pure, healthy, viable and weed-free.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Steps in planting a fruit orchard
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of planting a fruit orchard in the correct order.
(A) Marking the planting positions according to the layout
(B) Planting the sapling and watering it
(C) Digging pits and leaving them open to the sun
(D) Filling the pits with topsoil mixed with FYM
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (C), (D), (B)
Why: Positions are marked first (A), pits are dug and exposed to the sun (C), filled with topsoil and FYM (D), and the sapling is planted and watered (B).
Why not the others: Option (A) fills pits before digging them. Option (C) digs before marking. Option (D) plants before filling the pit.
Key point: Layout → pit → fill → plant.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question: Supporting tomato plants with bamboo sticks or wires so that the fruits stay off the ground is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) staking
Why: Staking holds the plant upright, keeps fruits clean and reduces rotting.
Why not the others: (A) earthing up heaps soil round the base; (B) thinning removes extra plants; (D) mulching covers the soil.
Key point: Staking for tomato and other tall vegetables.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Millets are small-seeded grasses that have been grown for grain since ancient times. At India's proposal, the United Nations declared 2023 the International Year of Millets, and in India millets were promoted as 'Shree Anna' and as 'nutri-cereals'. India is the world's largest producer of millets. They are grouped as major millets — sorghum (jowar), pearl millet (bajra) and finger millet (ragi) — and minor millets such as foxtail, kodo, little, proso and barnyard millet. Pearl millet is the most widely grown millet in India, and Rajasthan has the largest area under it. Millets are C₄ plants that use water efficiently. Most of them mature in 70–120 days and tolerate high temperature, drought and poor soils, so they suit rainfed drylands and need little fertilizer. A millet crop such as pearl millet needs only about 300 mm of water, while transplanted rice may need about 1,200 mm. Millets are rich in dietary fibre, in minerals such as iron and calcium, and in B vitamins. They are gluten-free and have a lower glycaemic index than polished rice, so they release sugar into the blood slowly. Their tiny seeds, hard seed coat and the short shelf life of their flour after milling have, however, limited their use, and better processing machines are being developed. Millet straw is also valued as fodder for animals.

Question: According to the passage, which year did the United Nations declare the International Year of Millets?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 2023
Why: The passage says the UN declared 2023 the International Year of Millets at India's proposal.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not the year given.
Key point: 2023 — International Year of Millets.

Question: Which of the following is a minor millet, as grouped in the passage?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Kodo millet
Why: The passage lists foxtail, kodo, little, proso and barnyard millet as minor millets.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are named as the major millets.
Key point: Major — jowar, bajra, ragi; the rest are minor millets.

Question: Why, according to the passage, are millets suited to rainfed drylands?
options: A) They are water-efficient C₄ plants that mature quickly and tolerate drought and poor soils
B) They grow only under standing water and need heavy doses of nitrogen fertilizer
C) They are long-duration crops that must be transplanted from a raised nursery
D) They are grown mainly for their oil and need assured canal irrigation to set seed
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) They are water-efficient C₄ plants that mature quickly and tolerate drought and poor soils
Why: The passage says millets are water-efficient C₄ plants, mature in 70–120 days and tolerate heat, drought and poor soils.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) contradict the passage.
Key point: Millets are climate-resilient dryland crops.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Water saved by replacing rice with millet
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Question: Using the water needs given in the passage, how much water (in cubic metres) is saved on one hectare by growing pearl millet instead of transplanted rice? (1 mm of water over 1 ha = 10 m³)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 9,000 m³
Why: Step 1: difference in water need = 1,200 − 300 = 900 mm.
Step 2: 900 mm × 10 m³ per mm per ha = 9,000 m³.
Why not the others: (A) forgets to multiply by 10; (B) multiplies by 100; (D) adds the two needs.
Key point: 1 mm over 1 ha = 10 m³.

questions.sub_topic: Claim that contradicts the millet text
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Question: A student sums up the passage in four claims. Which claim goes against what the passage says?
options: A) Millets can help people who must avoid gluten
B) Millet flour does not keep well for long after milling
C) Millets can be grown with little fertilizer
D) Millets need assured irrigation to give any yield
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Millets need assured irrigation to give any yield
Why: The passage says millets tolerate drought and suit rainfed drylands, so the claim that they need assured irrigation goes against it.
Why not the others: (A) matches 'gluten-free'; (B) matches 'short shelf life of their flour'; (C) matches 'need little fertilizer'.
Key point: Millets are rainfed crops; a NOT question asks for the claim the text contradicts.
